data.limitations: Runs occurred at different times and are not interleaved. Provider drift/load and embedding cache timing are confounds. Six-family intervals are exploratory, not independent population evidence. Missing tokens/costs remain unavailable. Native safety and answer accuracy are separate. No automatic winner or deployment.

limitations: Authored bounded lifecycle workload, six dependent families at two fictional-background lengths; not LoCoMo or LongMemEval scores.
Baseline reader protocols are standardized for exact values; this is not free-form conversation evaluation.
Middleware common-reader arms use the frozen interpreter and executor but replace response rendering with the same benchmark reader used by baselines.
Middleware selected/all-visible arms share one ingestion trace; each is charged the full interpreter cost for standalone attribution. Do not sum attributed costs across arms as actual billing.
Dense/hybrid arms share cached CPU embeddings; embedding build/query timing is recorded separately and must be included in standalone deployment analysis.
Each episode is independent; no conversation history from other episodes is provided.
Unsupported arbitrary fields, neural storage, multi-hop graph reasoning and exact secure erasure are not evaluated.
Native Mem0, Graphiti and Letta are not executed; no competitive product superiority claim.
Provider aliases can change; one scheduled generation per request, no retries or format repair.
Token counts are provider-reported when available. Missing metadata stays null. Monetary totals require supplied prices and are hypothetical token pricing, not subscription invoices.
Wall clock includes network/service time; provider timing is separate. Nonstreaming mode cannot measure time to first token.
Six-cluster intervals are exploratory; no significance or publication novelty claim.
